svg.title: A32: myeloid ARG1, matrix production and mature epithelial recovery
svg.desc: Hypothesis illustration. Proposed perturbation-effect comparison with separately measured matrix and absolute lineage-derived mature epithelial output. No measured effects or directional epithelial prediction are depicted.
svg.text: A32 / PROPOSED EFFECT QUESTION — NO EMPIRICAL RESULT
Does reducing myeloid ARG1 change matrix production
and mature epithelial recovery differently?
QUALIFIED SOURCE COMPARISON
Source-restricted myeloid ARG1 reduction versus matched source-active control
Non-infectious lung-repair system; actual donors/animals and declared nesting
One linked biological design; cell and well counts do not create independent units
MATRIX ENDPOINT
Newly produced or deposited collagen
Keep viable source and recipient amount
distinct from the matrix measurement.
EPITHELIAL ENDPOINT
Absolute lineage-derived mature AT1
output per starting epithelial input;
qualify lineage and mature function.
No epithelial direction is inferred from collagen alone.
READOUT → PERMITTED CONCLUSION
Less collagen + more mature output: favorable joint response; mediation unresolved.
Less collagen + less mature output: possible tradeoff; assess source/recipient loss.
Unresolved mature effect: retain uncertainty; nonsignificance is not preservation.
MAIN VALIDITY THREATS
Source depletion, changed inflammation, direct recipient exposure or selection
can mimic restored niche support. Separate early survival/expansion from maturation.
SPECIFIC HOLDS BEFORE EMPIRICAL WORK
Accessible model / linked data • source attribution • mature assay and timing
Independent-unit variance and meaningful precision; no invented margin or sample size
Qualitative hypothesis illustration • Proposed arrows and comparisons • Yd1-P02 source evidence remains separate
